title: Bevrijdingslinde van Jordaankinderen, the children's liberation tree
check_note: Sources differ on the urn: the Wijkkrant says it holds the names of the children who did not survive, the 4 and 5 May committee the names of the pupils who raised the money.

title: Canvas van Amsterdam on the Haringpakkersbrug, where the Haringpakkerstoren stood
check_note: The work up now is not confirmed; Hedy Tjin's was announced for September 2026.

title: De Poezenboot, the cat boat on the Singel
check_note: Hours and the closure from 25 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 come from the boat's site; confirm on the day.

title: Geldersekade 105 and the raid of 26 May 1943
check_note: One account says the photo shows the door of no. 105 being kicked in, but the photo is dated 26 May 1943 and the couple at no. 105 died on 21 May; match the photo to the houses on site.

title: Hofje Venetiae
check_note: Check the name at the street door, Elandsstraat 106: VENETIA cut in big letters, or an enamel VENETIAE plate (seen in 2025)?

title: Keizersgracht 516, Bodon's glass bookshop
check_note: After Borzo left (June 2021) the space hosted short exhibitions as Art Space Keizersgracht 516 (June 2022, May 2024, Instagram). Use in 2026 not found.

title: Lokaal 't Loosje and its brewery tile wall
check_note: The horse-tram waiting room and the origin of the name rest on the café's own account; an archive photo or tram history would settle them.

title: Metz & Co, the New York building and Rietveld's glass room on the roof
check_note: Which shop uses Keizersgracht 455 since Abercrombie & Fitch left at the end of 2022, and whether Rietveld's roof room can be visited

title: Pakketpostgebouw, the parcel machine beside Centraal Station
check_note: Current use not confirmed; the register (2004) says the railways (NS) used it after 1968. Check what is inside now.

title: Rozengracht bridges and the tram to Zandvoort
check_note: Bridge 167 renovated; 117 partly open since 26 Oct 2026 (AT5), trams 1 Mar 2027, done by 2029; 63 unfinished end 2025 (Mobilis). Is the rail stub on 167 still there?

title: Swigtershofje
check_note: Chapel confirmed as a guest suite (Nov 2026). Owner and use since 2018 (then De Key) not confirmed, nor whether the gate is ever open.

title: Torensluis, the bridge that carried a tower
check_note: Whether the cells under the bridge are still used for exhibitions or events, and how to get in.

title: Vijzelstraat, the street they widened by tearing down one side
check_note: The register calls Vijzelstraat 66-80 the former ABN AMRO office; check what it is used for now.

title: Zuid-Afrikahuis, the library whose books were thrown in the canal
check_note: Confirm the double-headed eagle is visible on the front and that the reading room is on the ground floor.

title: De Naaister and the corn measure, Bergstraat
check_note: The pin is at Bergstraat 6; place the statue exactly on site.

title: Kattenburgerplein, the old fronts that are new
check_note: Which numbers form the reconstructed row is not stated in the sources; pin at nos. 56-59, where the stone De Groenne Oven is.

title: Lindengracht, the filled canal and the eel riot
check_note: The pin is on the Lindengracht; where exactly the Zaterdagse brug crossed, and so where the eel hung, is not settled.

title: Nieuwezijds Kolk, the castle under the street
check_note: No marker known; pin from the dig plan on the Kolk. Check on site for any sign in the paving.

title: Prinseneiland: the last tar winch, the Palmentuin and Mandela's garden
check_note: Pin on the quay by the Sloterdijkerbrug; confirm the exact spot of the winch cover, and that the Mandela mural (last photographed 2021 and 2022) is still there.

title: The Dam shooting of 7 May 1945 and its 32 name stones
check_note: Pin on the 4en5mei point for the stones; the 1947 plaque is on the corner of the Kalverstraat.

title: The bicycle garage under the water at Stationsplein
check_note: Pin on the garage itself; the spot of the Lex Horn walls inside is not known.

title: The poor-relief bakery on the burned theatre's site
check_note: The register point lies inside the block, reached by the alley beside no. 495; whether the front with the time verse can be seen from a public spot was not checked.

title: Tip Top, the Jewish quarter's theatre (gone)
check_note: Pin placed on the old theatre site; set it on the stained-glass windows in the academy's front once seen

title: Walk of Pride, queer names from the Dam to the Homomonument
check_note: Pin at the Dam end of the Raadhuisstraat; fix it on Jillis Bruggeman's first tile. Sources give 52 or 53 tiles.

title: Café Theo Ruiter, the resistance man's literary bar
check_note: Is there still a café at Rozengracht 160, and under what name? Sources stop at 1980 for Café Theo Ruiter; no current status found.

title: De Aardige Amsterdammer, a hand for the volunteers
check_note: The hand was reported damaged in May 2024; whether it has been repaired is not known.

title: Electric Ladyland, a fluorescent cave where visitors push the buttons
check_note: The latest dated report is from 2016; the website still takes appointments. Confirm the museum still opens.

title: Keuken van 1870, the soup kitchen of the Spuistraat
check_note: A restaurant has used the ground floor since late 2012 (2017 source); check that a restaurant is still open and what it is called.

title: O Johnny, the gaper that replaced a gaper
check_note: Drugstore Het Heertje closed in spring 2024; the gaper was photographed in June 2024. Confirm it still hangs.

title: Singel 458, the Mennonite nurses' house
check_note: Hotel use is from the register (listed 2006, register name Haussmann); check that it is still a hotel.

title: The Kogelbron, a granite ball floating on water
check_note: Photographed in October 2018; check the fountain still runs and the ball still turns.

title: The first Tooneelschool building, Marnixstraat 150
check_note: Studios confirmed by nl.wikipedia (2023) and amsterdamopdekaart.nl (last updated November 2025); nothing later found 24 Nov 2026.

title: The one-of-a-kind cable box in the Langestraat
check_note: Listed in 2013; no recent report that the box is still on the pavement, and whether Zimmer's name is visible was not checked.

title: Tkramrepus, the reverse supermarket in the Czaar Peterstraat
check_note: Latest dated evidence is the crowdfunding of July 2024; confirm the shop is still open.

title: Volkskoffiehuis on the Kadijksplein
check_note: Pizzeria SOTTO went bankrupt 1 May 2026, closed, fittings auctioned (curator, 1 Oct 2026). New use unknown; is the Volksbond name still on the front?
